title: Playing with sounds and letters
summary: Practise the sounds in Spanish words and the letters that represent them.
keyIdeas: Spanish letters represent sounds. Some letters can represent different sounds, and h is silent.
Words are made by joining sounds in an order.
Changing a sound can make another Spanish word: pata and gata.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas la producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: Lucía plays at break time. Which Spanish word starts with the sound /p/?
activities.explanation: Pelota begins with p, representing /p/. Mesa begins with /m/, and gato with /g/.
activities.hint: Put your lips together before saying the first sound.

activities.prompt: The Spanish word «sol» has three sounds: /s/, /o/, /l/.
Complete the Spanish word with its first sound's letter.
activities.explanation: The word is gato. It starts with g, representing /g/.
activities.sentence: El animal que dice miau es el ___ato.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish words by their final sound.
activities.explanation: Casa, luna and pera end in /a/. Sapo, pato and barco end in /o/.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish word to its first letter.
activities.explanation: Sopa starts with S, Luna with L, Mano with M, and Tomate with T.

activities.prompt: Put the sounds in order to form the Spanish word «pan».
Find the Spanish sentence with a word misspelt by changing a sound.
activities.explanation: The fruit is called pera and starts with /p/. Writing bera with b changes the sound and is a spelling mistake.
activities.hint: Look at the word for the juicy green fruit.

activities.prompt: Aisha slowly counts the sounds in the Spanish word «mesa». How many are there?
Read the Spanish text carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Noticing sounds at the start and end of words helps us read.
activities.title: El perro de Mateo
activities.text:
El perro de Mateo se llama Tobi.
Tobi corre por el jardín.
Le gusta jugar con una pelota.
Mateo silba y Tobi viene.

questions.prompt: Which word in the text starts with /p/?
questions.explanation: Pelota and perro start with p, representing /p/.

questions.prompt: Which word in the text ends in /o/?
questions.explanation: Mateo ends in o, representing /o/. Jardín ends in /n/, and viene in /e/.

activities.prompt: Change the first sound of «pata» to form the Spanish name for another animal.
activities.explanation: Changing /p/ to /g/ makes gata, the Spanish word for a female cat.
